2: aṁśena iti — the word ‘aṁśena’; pratītya — according to the understood sense; abhiprāyeṇa — with the intended meaning; uktam — is stated.
3: nanu — but surely; uktāni — these have been stated; jātaḥ — born; gataḥ — went; pitṛ-gṛhāt — from the father’s house; vrajam — to Vraja; edhita-arthaḥ — with purpose fulfilled; ity-ādinā — by such statements and so on; satyam — true; punaḥ — again; vistareṇa — in detail; vada — speak; iti āha — thus he says; avatīrya iti — by the verse beginning ‘avatīrya.’
4: atra loke — in this world; tri-vidhāḥ janāḥ — three kinds of people; muktāḥ — liberated persons; mumukṣavaḥ — seekers of liberation; viṣayiṇaḥ ca — and material enjoyers; teṣām madhye — among them; atra — here; na kasyāpi — of none at all; alam-pratyayaḥ — a sense of ‘enough’; iti āha — thus he says; nivṛtta-tarṣaiḥ iti — by the words ‘nivṛtta-tarṣaiḥ’; gata-tṛṣṇaiḥ — by those whose thirst has gone; muktaiḥ — by liberated persons; iti arthaḥ — this is the meaning; mumukṣūṇām — for seekers of liberation; ayam eva upāyaḥ — this alone is the means; iti āha — thus he says; bhava-auṣadhāt iti — by the words ‘bhava-auṣadhāt’; viṣayiṇām — for material enjoyers; paramaḥ viṣayaḥ — the supreme object of enjoyment; ayam eva — this alone; iti āha — thus he says; śrotra-manaḥ-abhirāmāt iti — by the words ‘pleasing to ear and mind’; apagata śuk yasmāt — from whom sorrow has departed; tam ātmānam hanti — he kills that self; iti apaśu-ghnaḥ — thus ‘apaśu-ghna’; tasmāt — from him; paśu-ghātinaḥ iti vā — or, ‘from an animal-killer.’
5: kiṁ ca — moreover; asmat-kula-daivatam — the deity of our family; kṛṣṇaḥ — Kṛṣṇa; ataḥ — therefore; tat-kathā eva — His narration alone; nityam — always; śrotavyā — is to be heard; iti āśayena — with this intention; āha — he says; pitāmahāḥ iti — by ‘pitāmahāḥ’; amarān jayanti ye — those who conquer the immortals; taiḥ — by them; deva-vrataḥ — Devavrata; bhīṣmaḥ — Bhīṣma; tat-ādyaiḥ — beginning with him; atirathaiḥ — by great chariot-warriors; timiṅgilaiḥ — like timiṅgila monsters; timiṅgila-tulyaiḥ — equal to timiṅgilas; duratyayam — very difficult to cross; vatsa-padam iva — like a calf’s hoof-print; ati-alpam kṛtvā — making it extremely small; tucchīkṛtya — making it insignificant; ataran sma — they crossed; yaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ eva — that very Śrī Kṛṣṇa who; plavaḥ — the boat; yeṣām — of whom; te — they; tasya vīryāṇi — His heroic deeds; vadasva — speak; iti — thus; tṛtīya-śloka-gatena — by what is contained in the third verse; anvayaḥ — the connection.
6: na kevalam — not only; pāṇḍavān eva — the Pāṇḍavas alone; arakṣat — He protected; idam mama śarīram api — this body of mine also; yaḥ rakṣitavān — He who protected; iti āha — thus he says; drauṇi-astra-vipluṣṭam iti — by ‘scorched by Droṇa’s son’s weapon’; drauṇeḥ aśvatthāmnaḥ — of Aśvatthāmā, son of Droṇa; brahmāstreṇa — by the brahmāstra; dagdham — burned; idam mat-śarīram — this body of mine; ca — and; kurūṇām pāṇḍavānām ca — of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas; santānasya nidānam — the source of continuation; mama mātuḥ kukṣau — into my mother’s womb; praviṣṭaḥ — having entered; dhṛta-cakraḥ — holding the disc; yaḥ — who; jugopa — protected; iti — thus.
7: akhila-deha-bhājām — of all embodied beings; sarva-prāṇinām — of all living beings; antaḥ ca — within also; bahiḥ ca — outside also; puruṣa-rūpeṇa — in the form of the Puruṣa; kāla-rūpaiḥ ca — and in the forms of Time; aṁśa-abhiprāyeṇa — with reference to divisions; bahu-vacanam — the plural number; mṛtyum — death; saṁsāram — worldly existence; uta — and also; amṛtam api — immortality also; prayacchataḥ — of Him who bestows; vīryāṇi — heroic deeds; vadasva — speak; brūhi — tell; ayam bhāvaḥ — this is the purport; antaryāmi-rūpeṇa — in the form of the Inner Controller; antar-dṛṣṭīnām — to those whose vision is inward; muktim — liberation; bahiḥ-dṛṣṭīnām ca — and to those whose vision is outward; kāla-rūpeṇa — in the form of Time; mṛtyum — death; dadāti — gives; yataḥ — because; ataḥ — therefore; antar-dṛṣṭyā — with inward vision; tat-vīryāṇi eva — His heroic deeds alone; śrotavyāni — are to be heard; iti — thus.
